## Agent-based models extended session — Day 3, Session 2

Worksheet: `worksheets/10-agent-based-models-extended-session.qmd`. The chapter
is [Agent-based models](../chapters/09-agent-based-models.qmd).

Eight replicates separate effects of the size seen here, where the rules differ
by hundreds of infections, and are nowhere near enough to argue about
differences of a few tens. Every conclusion below is a statement about these
eight seeded runs at these settings.

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-setup
using Agents
using CairoMakie
using Distributions
using Random
using StableRNGs
using Statistics

function check(name, condition)
    condition || error("check failed: $name")
    println("✓ $name")
    return nothing
end

N = 1000
β = 0.05
c = 10.0
γ = 0.25

@agent struct Person(GridAgent{2})
    status::Symbol
    next_status::Symbol
end

susceptible_count(model) = count(p.status == :S for p in allagents(model))
infected_count(model) = count(p.status == :I for p in allagents(model))
recovered_count(model) = count(p.status == :R for p in allagents(model))
```

### Part A — agents who react

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-a1
function is_aware(person, model)
    if model.information == :none
        return false
    elseif model.information == :national
        return model.prevalence >= model.θ
    elseif model.information == :local
        return count(a -> a.status == :I,
                     nearby_agents(person, model, model.info_radius)) >= model.m
    else
        throw(ArgumentError(
            "unknown information rule $(model.information); " *
            "expected :none, :local or :national"))
    end
end
```

All three rules are named and anything else raises. With `:local` as a bare
`else`, a typo such as `information = :locl` would silently select the local
rule and the run would look healthy.

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-a2
function agent_step!(person, model)
    person.next_status = person.status
    if person.status == :S
        transmission = is_aware(person, model) ? model.β * (1 - model.α) : model.β
        neighbours = collect(nearby_agents(person, model, model.radius))
        for _ in 1:rand(abmrng(model), Poisson(model.c * model.Δt))
            contact = rand(abmrng(model), neighbours)
            if contact.status == :I && rand(abmrng(model)) < transmission
                person.next_status = :I
                break
            end
        end
    elseif person.status == :I
        if rand(abmrng(model)) < 1 - exp(-model.γ * model.Δt)
            person.next_status = :R
        end
    end
    return nothing
end

function model_step!(model)
    model.aware_days += model.Δt *
        count(p -> p.status == :S && is_aware(p, model), allagents(model))
    for person in allagents(model)
        person.status = person.next_status
    end
    model.prevalence = infected_count(model) / N
    return nothing
end
```

Every awareness evaluation within a step sees the same pre-update state, and the
aware person-days are counted before the commit, so they count exactly the
people whose transmission `agent_step!` reduced.

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-a3
function initialize_model(seed; information = :none, α = 0.5, m = 1,
                          info_radius = 3, θ = 0.05,
                          I0 = 10, radius = 2, Δt = 0.1)
    space = GridSpaceSingle((40, 25); periodic = true, metric = :chebyshev)
    model = StandardABM(
        Person, space;
        agent_step!, model_step!,
        properties = Dict(
            :β => β, :c => c, :γ => γ, :Δt => Δt, :radius => radius,
            :information => information, :α => α, :m => m,
            :info_radius => info_radius, :θ => θ,
            :prevalence => I0 / N, :aware_days => 0.0,
        ),
        rng = StableRNG(seed),
    )
    for position in positions(model)
        add_agent!(position, model; status = :S, next_status = :S)
    end
    for id in shuffle(abmrng(model), collect(allids(model)))[1:I0]
        model[id].status = :I
        model[id].next_status = :I
    end
    return model
end

function run_epidemic(seed; max_steps = 10_000, kwargs...)
    model = initialize_model(seed; kwargs...)
    infectious = Int[infected_count(model)]
    while infectious[end] > 0
        length(infectious) > max_steps && error(
            "still infectious after $max_steps steps ($(max_steps * model.Δt) time " *
            "units); raise max_steps. A response too weak to interrupt transmission " *
            "can run far longer than the settings used here.")
        step!(model, 1)
        push!(infectious, infected_count(model))
    end
    return (; peak = maximum(infectious),
              final = recovered_count(model),
              aware_days = model.aware_days,
              duration = (length(infectious) - 1) * model.Δt,
              infectious)
end

replicate_seeds = 7000 .+ (1:8)

function summarise(; kwargs...)
    runs = [run_epidemic(seed; kwargs...) for seed in replicate_seeds]
    return (; peak = round(mean(r.peak for r in runs); digits = 1),
              final = round(mean(r.final for r in runs); digits = 1),
              final_sd = round(std([r.final for r in runs]); digits = 1),
              aware_days = round(Int, mean(r.aware_days for r in runs)),
              duration = round(mean(r.duration for r in runs); digits = 1),
              finals = [Float64(r.final) for r in runs],
              aware_each = [r.aware_days for r in runs])
end
```

`run_epidemic` runs until nobody is infectious, so every number it reports is a
final one, and the step cap raises rather than returning a half-finished epidemic.

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-a4
baseline = summarise(information = :none)
local_rule = summarise(information = :local, m = 1, α = 0.5)

check("awareness lowers the peak", local_rule.peak < 0.6 * baseline.peak)
check("awareness lowers the final size", local_rule.final < 0.5 * baseline.final)
check("the baseline population never takes precautions",
      baseline.aware_days == 0.0)

(; baseline, local_rule)
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-ws-ch06b-snapshot
#| fig-cap: "One run with the local rule, at three times. Blue is susceptible, orange is a susceptible person taking precautions, red infectious, green recovered. Precautions are concentrated around the infected patches rather than spread across the grid, which is what Part C then measures."
snapshot_model = initialize_model(7001; information = :local, m = 1, α = 0.5)
awareness_colour(p) =
    p.status === :I ? :firebrick :
    p.status === :R ? :seagreen :
    is_aware(p, snapshot_model) ? :orange : :steelblue

fig = Figure(size = (1000, 250))
previous = 0.0
for (j, t) in enumerate((3.0, 8.0, 20.0))
    step!(snapshot_model, round(Int, (t - previous) / 0.1))
    previous = t
    ax = Axis(fig[1, j]; title = "t = $t", aspect = DataAspect())
    abmplot!(ax, snapshot_model; agent_color = awareness_colour,
             agent_marker = :rect, agent_size = 7)
    hidedecorations!(ax)
end
fig
```

The two information radii are run in lockstep and compared agent by agent,
because equal S, I and R totals could still put different people in each
compartment.

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-a5
function compare_radii(seed; m, α = 0.5, radii = (3, 2), max_steps = 10_000)
    models = [initialize_model(seed; information = :local, m = m, α = α, info_radius = r)
              for r in radii]
    statuses(model) = [model[id].status for id in 1:nagents(model)]
    agree = statuses(models[1]) == statuses(models[2])
    steps = 0
    while any(infected_count(model) > 0 for model in models)
        steps += 1
        steps > max_steps && error("still infectious after $max_steps steps; raise max_steps")
        foreach(model -> step!(model, 1), models)
        agree &= statuses(models[1]) == statuses(models[2])
    end
    return (; agree,
              final = map(recovered_count, models),
              aware_days = map(model -> model.aware_days, models))
end

comparisons = Dict(m => [compare_radii(seed; m = m) for seed in replicate_seeds]
                   for m in (1, 2))

check("at m = 1 every agent holds the same status at every step under both radii",
      all(c.agree for c in comparisons[1]))
check("the two radii still record different amounts of precaution",
      all(c.aware_days[1] > c.aware_days[2] for c in comparisons[1]))
check("at m = 2 the two populations diverge, in every seed",
      all(!c.agree for c in comparisons[2]))

[(; m,
    final_info_radius_3 = round(mean(c.final[1] for c in cs); digits = 1),
    final_info_radius_2 = round(mean(c.final[2] for c in cs); digits = 1),
    aware_days_3 = round(Int, mean(c.aware_days[1] for c in cs)),
    aware_days_2 = round(Int, mean(c.aware_days[2] for c in cs)))
 for (m, cs) in ((1, comparisons[1]), (2, comparisons[2]))]
```

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-a6
function paired_final_contrast(cs; reps = 4000, seed = 11)
    differences = [Float64(c.final[1] - c.final[2]) for c in cs]
    rng = StableRNG(seed)
    n = length(differences)
    resampled = map(1:reps) do _
        mean(differences[rand(rng, 1:n, n)])
    end
    return (; per_seed_difference = Int.(differences),
              mean_difference = round(mean(differences); digits = 1),
              seeds_favouring_radius_3 = count(<(0), differences),
              interval = (round(quantile(resampled, 0.025); digits = 1),
                          round(quantile(resampled, 0.975); digits = 1)))
end

paired_final_contrast(comparisons[2])
```

#### A1. Interpret

- At `m = 1` an information radius of 3 gives no advance warning over a contact
  radius of 2: every one of the thousand agents holds the same status at every
  step under both radii, in all eight seeds.
- The reason is a two-case split. If any of the twenty-four people within two
  cells is infectious, the person is aware under both radii, because the inner
  ring already supplies the one case `m = 1` asks for. If none is, no contact can
  transmit and the reduced $\beta$ is never used. `is_aware` draws no random
  numbers, so the two runs also stay in lockstep draw for draw.
- Awareness owed only to the outer ring is held by somebody with no infectious
  contact, and `is_aware` is recomputed every step, so nothing carries it
  forward. A memoryless rule has no "earlier" to warn from.
- What the outer ring changes is the accounting: about 4,533 aware person-days at
  `info_radius = 3` against 2,524 at `info_radius = 2`, for the same mean final
  size of 47.1. Against the radius-2 denominator the local rule averts 0.241
  infections per aware person-day rather than 0.134, so every later comparison on
  this measure is run in the local rule's disfavour.
- At `m = 2` the radii come apart in every seed, because a second case within
  three cells can now tip over the threshold a person who does have an infectious
  contact. The mean final size is 139.8 at radius 3 against 175.4 at radius 2, but
  the per-seed differences are 77, −38, 15, −163, −131, −28, 6 and −23 and the
  paired interval $(-86.6, 12.6)$ contains zero: the radius matters at `m = 2`,
  and these seeds do not establish that widening it helps.
- Genuine advance warning needs awareness with memory, or a response that takes
  effect some steps after the trigger. Both make awareness agent state, so the
  struct, the initialiser and both stepping functions change. Raising `m` is a
  one-line change that makes the outer ring consequential without warning anybody
  in advance.
- Nothing here makes precautions persist, so protection is withdrawn from people
  still susceptible. At $\alpha = 0.5$ the epidemic is over in about 26 time units
  against the baseline's 104; at $\alpha = 0.25$ it runs for about 93, with
  awareness switching on and off across the grid throughout.

### Part B — how soon, and how hard

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-b1
trigger_sweep = [(; m, summarise(information = :local, m = m, α = 0.5)...)
                 for m in (1, 2, 3)]
```

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-b2
strength_sweep = [(; α, summarise(information = :local, m = 1, α = α)...)
                  for α in (0.25, 0.5, 0.75)]
```

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-b3
# Use the per-seed vectors, not `final` and `aware_days`: `summarise` rounds those
# two for display, and the bootstrap below resamples the unrounded values, so the
# point estimate and its interval should be built from the same numbers.
averted_per_aware_day(result) =
    (mean(baseline.finals) - mean(result.finals)) / mean(result.aware_each)

check("a rule that changes nothing averts nothing",
      averted_per_aware_day((; finals = baseline.finals,
                               aware_each = ones(length(baseline.finals)))) == 0.0)
check("of the three triggers, acting on the first case has the highest point estimate",
      averted_per_aware_day(trigger_sweep[1]) >
      maximum(averted_per_aware_day(r) for r in trigger_sweep[2:end]))

[(; description = "m = $(r.m)", averted = round(averted_per_aware_day(r); digits = 3))
 for r in trigger_sweep]
```

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-b4
[(; description = "α = $(r.α)", averted = round(averted_per_aware_day(r); digits = 3))
 for r in strength_sweep]
```

Every setting shares `replicate_seeds`, so the bootstrap resamples the eight
seeds and recomputes the whole ratio from the seeds drawn, which keeps the
pairing with the baseline intact.

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-b5
function averted_interval(result; reps = 4000, seed = 11)
    rng = StableRNG(seed)
    n = length(result.finals)
    samples = map(1:reps) do _
        drawn = rand(rng, 1:n, n)
        taken = mean(result.aware_each[drawn])
        taken == 0 ? NaN :
            (mean(baseline.finals[drawn]) - mean(result.finals[drawn])) / taken
    end
    usable = filter(isfinite, samples)
    isempty(usable) && return nothing   # a rule nobody ever acts on has no ratio
    return (round(quantile(usable, 0.025); digits = 3),
            round(quantile(usable, 0.975); digits = 3))
end

[(; description = "m = $(r.m)",
    averted = round(averted_per_aware_day(r); digits = 3),
    interval = averted_interval(r)) for r in trigger_sweep]
```

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-b6
[(; description = "α = $(r.α)",
    averted = round(averted_per_aware_day(r); digits = 3),
    interval = averted_interval(r)) for r in strength_sweep]
```

A marginal interval answers whether one rule averts anything at all. Whether two
settings differ is a question about the contrast, so it is bootstrapped directly
from the same drawn seeds.

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-b7
function contrast_interval(first_rule, second_rule; reps = 4000, seed = 11)
    rng = StableRNG(seed)
    n = length(first_rule.finals)
    value(drawn, rule) = (mean(baseline.finals[drawn]) - mean(rule.finals[drawn])) /
                         mean(rule.aware_each[drawn])
    samples = map(1:reps) do _
        drawn = rand(rng, 1:n, n)
        value(drawn, first_rule) - value(drawn, second_rule)
    end
    usable = filter(isfinite, samples)
    isempty(usable) && return nothing
    return (round(quantile(usable, 0.025); digits = 3),
            round(quantile(usable, 0.975); digits = 3))
end

[(; contrast = "m = $(a.m) minus m = $(b.m)",
    difference = round(averted_per_aware_day(a) - averted_per_aware_day(b); digits = 3),
    interval = contrast_interval(a, b))
 for (a, b) in ((trigger_sweep[1], trigger_sweep[2]),
                (trigger_sweep[1], trigger_sweep[3]),
                (trigger_sweep[2], trigger_sweep[3]))]
```

```{julia}
#| label: ws-ch06b-b8
[(; contrast = "α = $(a.α) minus α = $(b.α)",
    difference = round(averted_per_aware_day(a) - averted_per_aware_day(b); digits = 3),
    interval = contrast_interval(a, b))
 for (a, b) in ((strength_sweep[3], strength_sweep[2]),
                (strength_sweep[2], strength_sweep[1]),
                (strength_sweep[3], strength_sweep[1]))]
```

#### B1. Interpret

- The weakest response asks most of the population. At $\alpha = 0.25$ it takes
  about 16,600 aware person-days and ends with 285 infections; at $\alpha = 0.75$
  about 2,300 and 17.5. Precaution is taken per person per unit time, and a
  response that breaks transmission ends the epidemic in about 13 time units,
  while one too weak to break it keeps the population alert for about 93. That is
  a finding about this model at these settings, not a general law.
- The standard deviation of final size is 98.9 at $\alpha = 0.25$ and 6.9 at
  $\alpha = 0.75$. The results are consistent with a move from mostly sustained to
  mostly interrupted transmission across the tested $\alpha$, and eight runs cannot
  locate it; the rule switches per person per step, so there is no single constant
  reproduction number to cross one. The wide spread is intrinsic outcome
  variability, not an unconverged calculation.
- Per-setting intervals (`ws-ch06b-b5`, `ws-ch06b-b6`) answer whether a rule
  averts anything; the contrasts (`ws-ch06b-b7`, `ws-ch06b-b8`) answer whether two
  settings differ. Overlapping marginal intervals are compatible with a contrast
  well clear of zero.
- Point estimates are 0.134 at $m = 1$, 0.096 at $m = 2$ and 0.080 at $m = 3$. The
  contrasts are $0.038\ (0.007,\ 0.082)$ for $m = 1$ minus $m = 2$,
  $0.055\ (-0.007,\ 0.129)$ for $m = 1$ minus $m = 3$ and $0.016\ (-0.035,\ 0.065)$
  for $m = 2$ minus $m = 3$. Only the first is separated, narrowly, which with eight
  seeds is suggestive; $m = 3$ has the most variable outcomes (122 to 440), so its
  contrasts are widest. There is no supported ranking of all three.
- The strength sweep is clear: $(0.059,\ 0.235)$ for $\alpha = 0.75$ against
  $0.5$, $(0.074,\ 0.172)$ for $0.5$ against $0.25$ and $(0.188,\ 0.345)$ end to
  end, all clear of zero, because the effect spans more than an order of
  magnitude.
- $\alpha$ is the number to argue about first: it sets the transmission
  reduction directly and is hard to estimate during an outbreak. `m` and
  `info_radius` need empirical grounding too. The model attaches no cost to an
  aware person-day, whether that is a mask or a missed shift, and assumes
  compliance is complete.

### Part C — the same behaviour, different information

At $\theta = 0.10$ the rule never activates, because the grid epidemic peaks at
about seventy infectious people out of a thousand; it records zero aware
person-days and behaves exactly as the baseline.

#### C1. Interpret

- At the matched setting the two rules take similar precaution, about 4,500
  aware person-days locally against about 3,900 nationally, and end at 47
  infections against 616. The precautions are identical; what differs is who
  takes them. A person-day of precaution does something only if it coincides with
  an exposure, and the local rule places its participation around current
  infection.
- At $\theta = 0.05$ the national rule averts 0.010 infections per aware
  person-day, marginal interval $(-0.013, 0.055)$, so these runs do not establish
  that it averts anything. The direct contrast in `ws-ch06b-c2b` has the local
  rule averting 0.124 more, interval $(0.088, 0.168)$, and `local_minus_this`
  carries the same contrast against every threshold.
- Duration is the other half: about 26 time units for the local rule against 112
  for the national one. The national rule switches off whenever prevalence falls
  back below $\theta$, which can be well before the epidemic ends.
- Writing the local rule as equations in $S$, $I$ and $R$ would need the number of
  susceptible people with at least one infectious neighbour, so the state would
  have to carry neighbourhood composition, and pair equations introduce triples.
  The national rule is a function of $I/N$ and can be written as $\beta(I)$ with no
  agents. Pairwise and message-passing models can carry the local configuration
  too, exactly on some networks; a model whose state is $S$, $I$ and $R$ totals
  cannot express the rule at all.
- Two failures of the information assumption both push against the local rule:
  people are infectious before they look ill, so warning arrives after exposure,
  and people see reported cases for an area after a delay, not their neighbours'
  status. The 47 against 616 is an optimistic benchmark for local information,
  not a forecast.
- The national rule at $\theta = 0.01$ reduces the epidemic from 656 to 174, for
  about 28,600 aware person-days, more than six times what the local rule takes to
  reach 47. Against it the
  local rule averts 0.117 more per aware person-day, interval $(0.080, 0.178)$.
  That survives eight seeds because the gap is large, even with the local rule's
  denominator inflated by an outer ring that does nothing at `m = 1`.
